스물.forms: native · counting things, age · before a counter: 스무 (스무 살) · 21+: 스물한 살
스물.x: My younger sibling is twenty years old.
스물.t: Alone before a counter it becomes 스무: 스무 살. With a unit digit it stays 스물: 스물두 살.

매일.t: 매 + time word means 'every': 매주 every week, 매달 every month, 매년 every year.

물건.x: This store has a lot of good items.

사진.x: May I take a photo here?

바람.e: Also means 'a wish' (from 바라다, to hope). 바람을 피우다 = to cheat on a partner.

구름.x: There isn't a single cloud in the sky.

함께.x: I live together with my parents.
함께.t: Same meaning as 같이, but a bit more formal or written.

치킨.x: Shall we order fried chicken for dinner tonight?
치킨.e: From English 'chicken', but in Korean it means fried chicken; chicken meat is 닭고기.
치킨.t: Can't decide? Order 반반: half 후라이드 (plain fried), half 양념 (sweet and spicy sauce).

부러지다.x: I fell while skiing and broke my leg.
부러지다.e: Used for long, hard things like bones or pencils; glass and dishes use 깨지다.
부러지다.t: Korean says 'my leg broke' (다리가 부러졌어요) where English says 'I broke my leg.'

글자.ex: 글자가 너무 작아서 잘 안 보여요.
글자.x: The letters are too small, so I can't see them well.

찌다.m: to steam; to gain weight (살이 찌다)
찌다.x: I steamed potatoes and gave them to the kids as a snack.
찌다.t: To gain weight is 살이 찌다; to lose weight is 살이 빠지다.

손녀.x: Grandpa read a storybook to his granddaughter.

시월.x: In October, the autumn leaves on the mountains are very pretty.
시월.e: 십 'ten' drops its ㅂ here: 시월, not 십월.

알아보다.m: to look into, to find out, to check; to recognize
알아보다.ex: 여행 가기 전에 호텔 가격을 알아봤어요.
알아보다.x: I checked hotel prices before the trip.

근무.ex: 우리 회사 근무 시간은 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지예요.
근무.x: Our company's working hours are from nine to six.

처리하다.m: to handle, to deal with, to process
처리하다.x: Please take care of this issue by today.

불편.x: We apologize for the inconvenience caused by the construction.
불편.t: 불편을 드려서 죄송합니다 is the standard formal apology for an inconvenience.

피해.ex: 이번 태풍으로 농촌에 큰 피해가 생겼습니다.
피해.x: This typhoon caused major damage to rural areas.
피해.t: 피해를 주다 'give harm' and 피해를 입다 'suffer harm' are the key collocations; 민폐 is a casual 'nuisance.'

자녀.x: Excuse me, but how many children do you have?
자녀.t: 자녀 is polite and formal; use it when asking about someone else's children.

신뢰.ex: 한 번 잃은 신뢰는 다시 얻기 어렵습니다.
신뢰.x: Trust, once lost, is hard to win back.

연고.x: I put ointment on the cut and stuck a bandage on it.

위반하다.m: to violate, to break (a rule or law)
위반하다.ex: 그 운전자는 신호를 위반해서 벌금을 냈어요.
위반하다.x: That driver ran a red light and paid a fine.
위반하다.e: Literally 'to go against and oppose' a rule.

위로.ex: 친구의 따뜻한 말이 큰 위로가 됐어요.
위로.x: My friend's warm words were a great comfort.
위로.t: Homonym: 위로 also means 'upward' (위 + 로), as in 위로 올라가세요.

미워하다.ex: 저는 그 사람을 이제 미워하지 않아요.
미워하다.x: I don't hate that person anymore.
미워하다.e: From 밉다 'hateful' plus -어하다, turning the feeling into a verb.

파다.m: to dig; to carve; to dig into (study deeply)
파다.x: The kids are digging in the sand at the beach and playing.
파다.t: Watch out: 팔 거예요 and 파세요 look the same as forms of 팔다 'to sell'; context decides.

퇴사.ex: 다음 달에 퇴사하고 잠시 쉬려고 해요.
퇴사.x: I'm going to leave the company next month and take a short break.
퇴사.e: Literally 'leaving the company'. Opposite: 입사 'joining a company'.
퇴사.t: 퇴사 is quitting for good, while 퇴근 is just leaving work for the day. Verb: 퇴사하다.

교대.x: This factory works around the clock in three shifts.
교대.t: 교대 is also the short name for 교육대학교, a teachers' college.

자영업.ex: 우리 부모님은 이십 년 동안 자영업을 하셨어요.
자영업.x: My parents ran their own business for twenty years.

저자.x: The author of this book is a famous scientist.
저자.e: -자 = person who does it: 저자, 과학자, 운전자.
저자.t: 저자 is the author of a specific book; 작가 is a writer or artist by profession.

까칠하다.ex: 그 사람은 처음엔 까칠해 보였지만 사실 착해요.
까칠하다.x: He seemed prickly at first, but he's actually nice.
까칠하다.e: Originally 'rough, dry' skin — extended to a prickly personality.

권유하다.m: to recommend, to invite, to urge (someone to do something)
권유하다.x: My friend urged me to work out together.

호소하다.m: to appeal, to plead; to complain of (pain)
호소하다.x: The patient had been complaining of a severe headache since yesterday.

단순하다.ex: 이 게임은 규칙이 단순해서 누구나 할 수 있어요.
단순하다.x: This game has simple rules, so anyone can play.

초라하다.ex: 친구들 앞에서 제 모습이 너무 초라하게 느껴졌어요.
초라하다.x: I felt really shabby in front of my friends.

희귀하다.ex: 이 새는 아주 희귀해서 보기 힘들어요.
희귀하다.x: This bird is very rare, so it's hard to spot.
희귀하다.t: Pronounced [히귀하다] — the vowel ㅢ after a consonant sounds like ㅣ.

비위를 맞추다.forms: 비위를 맞춰요 · 비위를 맞췄어요 · N의 비위를 맞추다
비위를 맞추다.m: to humor someone, to cater to someone's moods, to please
비위를 맞추다.ex: 그는 사장님의 비위를 맞추느라 늘 피곤해요.
비위를 맞추다.x: He's always tired from catering to the boss's moods.
비위를 맞추다.e: Literally 'to match someone's spleen and stomach,' meaning their tastes and moods.

걸레.ex: 청소할 때 걸레로 바닥을 깨끗하게 닦았어요.
걸레.x: When I cleaned, I wiped the floor with a rag.
걸레.t: 걸레 is for floors; a cloth for dishes or tables is 행주, so don't mix them up.

스포일러.ex: 스포일러를 볼까 봐 댓글을 안 읽어요.
스포일러.x: I don't read the comments in case I see spoilers.
스포일러.e: From English 'spoiler'; usually shortened to 스포.
스포일러.t: Casual: 스포하지 마! 'Don't spoil it!' 스포 주의 'spoiler alert' appears at the top of posts.

로코.ex: 주말에 가볍게 볼 로코 좀 추천해 주세요.
로코.x: Please recommend a light rom-com to watch on the weekend.
로코.e: Clipped from 로맨틱 코미디 'romantic comedy', like English 'rom-com'.
로코.t: Casual. 로코 장인 'rom-com master' is praise for an actor known for the genre.

방긋.m: with a sweet little smile (esp. a baby)
방긋.x: The baby looks at its mom and smiles sweetly.
방긋.e: Manner word (의태어) for a soft smile with the mouth slightly open. Dark-vowel 벙긋 is a bigger, wider smile.
방긋.t: Pronounced [방귿]: a final ㅅ sounds like ㄷ. 방긋방긋 means smiling again and again; 방긋거리다 also exists.

평정심.ex: 어려운 상황에서도 평정심을 잃지 않는 것이 중요해요.
평정심.x: It's important not to lose your composure even in hard situations.

도발.ex: 정부는 상대의 군사 도발에 단호하게 대응하겠다고 밝혔습니다.
도발.x: The government said it would respond firmly to the military provocation.
도발.e: Literally 'challenge and set off' — stirring up a fight.
도발.t: 도발적 can also mean 'provocative' in style or fashion, like a bold outfit.

폐쇄하다.ex: 경찰은 사고 현장 주변 도로를 폐쇄했습니다.
폐쇄하다.x: The police closed the roads around the accident scene.
폐쇄하다.t: 폐쇄적 describes a closed, exclusive attitude: 폐쇄적인 사회 'a closed society.'

모순되다.m: to be contradictory, to be inconsistent
모순되다.x: His words and actions contradict each other.
모순되다.e: From a Chinese tale: a seller boasting of an unstoppable spear and an unbreakable shield.

전수하다.m: to pass down, to hand down (skills, know-how)
전수하다.ex: 할아버지는 평생 익힌 기술을 손자에게 전수했어요.
전수하다.x: Grandfather passed down the skills he had mastered over his lifetime to his grandson.
전수하다.e: Literally 'transmit and give' — teaching someone your craft.

쇠퇴하다.m: to decline, to wane, to decay
쇠퇴하다.ex: 석탄 산업이 쇠퇴하면서 많은 광산 마을이 비었어요.
쇠퇴하다.x: As the coal industry declined, many mining towns emptied out.

여간.forms: 여간 + adj + -지 않다 · 여간 -ㄴ 게 아니다 (= very)
여간.m: (with a negative) extremely, no ordinary, not a little
여간.ex: 혼자서 아이 셋을 키우는 건 여간 힘든 일이 아니에요.
여간.x: Raising three kids alone is no easy job.
여간.e: Always paired with a negative to mean the opposite: 'not a little' means 'very'.
여간.t: 여간 어렵지 않다 means 'extremely difficult', not 'not difficult'.

천고마비.m: crisp autumn weather; autumn, when the sky is high and horses grow fat
천고마비.ex: 하늘이 높고 맑은 천고마비의 계절이 왔어요.
천고마비.x: The season of high, clear skies and plump horses has arrived.
천고마비.e: Literally 'the sky is high, the horses are fat'.
천고마비.t: Almost always 천고마비의 계절, a stock phrase for Korean autumn.

의식적.ex: 요즘 의식적으로 물을 많이 마시려고 해요.
의식적.x: These days I'm making a conscious effort to drink a lot of water.
의식적.e: From 의식 'consciousness' + -적 '-al'. -적 turns nouns into adjectives: 사회적, 문화적.
의식적.t: Most often used as the adverb 의식적으로, meaning 'consciously, on purpose'.

향학열.m: zeal for learning, eagerness to study
향학열.ex: 그 할머니의 향학열은 젊은 사람 못지않아요.
향학열.x: That elderly woman's zeal for learning is as strong as any young person's.
향학열.t: Pronounced [향항녈] — an ㄴ is added, then nasalization.

비몽사몽.m: being half asleep, half awake; in a daze
비몽사몽.ex: 비몽사몽간에 전화를 받아서 기억이 하나도 안 나요.
비몽사몽.x: I answered the phone half asleep, so I don't remember a thing.
비몽사몽.e: Literally 'not a dream, yet like a dream' — the hazy state between sleeping and waking.
비몽사몽.t: Common in everyday talk: 비몽사몽간에 'while half asleep', 아직 비몽사몽이에요 'I'm still not fully awake'.

무더위 쉼터.m: cooling shelter (public place to escape the heat)
무더위 쉼터.ex: 더위가 심할 때는 동네 무더위 쉼터에서 쉬세요.
무더위 쉼터.x: When the heat is severe, rest at a cooling shelter in your neighborhood.
무더위 쉼터.e: Native words: 무더위 'sweltering heat' + 쉼터 'resting place' (쉬다 'to rest' + 터 'site').
무더위 쉼터.t: Local governments designate air-conditioned places such as senior centers (경로당) and community service centers as 무더위 쉼터 every summer, mainly for elderly people; they are free to use.

절세.m: tax saving (legal ways to pay less tax)
절세.ex: 연말정산 때 절세 방법을 미리 알아 두세요.
절세.x: Learn some tax-saving tips ahead of your year-end tax settlement.
절세.e: Literally 'economizing on tax' — legal, unlike 탈세 'tax evasion.'
절세.t: Pronounced [절쎄]: ㅅ becomes tense after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

철군.x: The government announced it would complete the troop withdrawal by the end of the year.

이차전지.x: Electric cars use high-capacity rechargeable batteries.
이차전지.e: Literally 'second-round battery' — it can be recharged and reused.
이차전지.t: In business news, 이차전지 often refers to the whole EV battery industry.

열사.ex: 유관순 열사는 삼일운동에 참여했다가 감옥에서 세상을 떠났어요.
열사.x: The martyr Yu Gwan-sun took part in the March 1st Movement and died in prison.
열사.t: 열사 resisted without weapons, like 유관순 열사; 의사 used armed action, like 안중근 의사.

노발대발.m: flying into a rage, being furious
노발대발.x: My father flew into a rage when he heard the news.
노발대발.e: Literally 'anger bursts out, bursts out big.'
노발대발.t: Often used with honorifics about elders or bosses: 사장님이 노발대발하셨다.

폄하하다.m: to belittle, to disparage, to play down
폄하하다.ex: 남의 노력을 폄하하는 것은 좋지 않아요.
폄하하다.x: It's not good to belittle other people's efforts.
폄하하다.e: Literally 'lower the rank' of someone or something.

무모하다.ex: 준비 없이 겨울 산에 오르는 것은 무모해요.
무모하다.x: Climbing a mountain in winter without preparation is reckless.

일체.x: The company covers all travel expenses.
일체.t: 일체 = all (positive), 일절 = not at all (negative): 일체 무료 vs 일절 금지.

낙인찍다.m: to brand, to stigmatize, to label
낙인찍다.e: Literally 'press a branding iron': marking someone with a lasting stigma.
낙인찍다.t: Pattern: A를 B(으)로 낙인찍다. The passive 낙인찍히다 is very common.

하달하다.m: to pass down (orders), to issue (instructions to subordinates)
하달하다.ex: 본부는 각 지점에 새로운 지침을 하달했습니다.
하달하다.x: Headquarters passed down new guidelines to every branch.
하달하다.e: Literally 'send down to reach' — orders flowing from the top.

회유하다.m: to coax, to conciliate, to win over (with soft words or favors)
회유하다.x: He tried to win the witness over with money.
회유하다.e: Literally 'embrace softly' — persuading through gentleness instead of force.
회유하다.t: Often paired with its opposite: 회유와 협박 'carrots and sticks'.

우매하다.ex: 우매한 결정 때문에 회사가 큰 손해를 입었습니다.
우매하다.x: The company suffered a huge loss because of a foolish decision.

현묘하다.ex: 동양 철학에는 현묘한 이치가 담겨 있다고 해요.
현묘하다.x: They say Eastern philosophy holds profound and subtle truths.
현묘하다.e: Literally 'dark and wondrous' — too deep to fully grasp.

정겹다.x: The scenery of the country village is so warm and homey.
정겹다.t: Often describes familiar sights and sounds: 정겨운 사투리, 정겨운 골목.

자강불식.x: I study every day with an attitude of never ceasing to improve myself.
자강불식.e: From the Book of Changes: strengthen yourself and never stop.

대손.x: The bank set aside reserves to prepare for bad debts.
대손.e: Literally 'lending loss' — money lent that won't come back.
대손.t: Mostly appears in accounting terms like 대손충당금 and 대손상각.
